title: Running Median
statement:
Maintain the median of a growing stream of integers.

Contract
- Implement an instance class with `void add(int value)` and `double median()`. A new instance starts with no values.
- `add` accepts any `int`, including negatives, duplicates, `Integer.MIN_VALUE` and `Integer.MAX_VALUE`.
- `median` returns the middle value of everything added so far, or the average of the two middle values when the count is even. The average must be exact even for values near the `int` limits.
- `median` throws `IllegalStateException` when no value has been added yet.
- `median` may be called any number of times between additions and must not change the result.

Examples
- After adding 5, 15 and 1 the medians are 5.0, 10.0 and 5.0 after each addition.
- Calling `median()` on a new instance throws `IllegalStateException`.
- After adding -1, -1, 4 and 4 the medians are -1.0, -1.0, -1.0 and 1.5.

examples.input: add 5, median, add 15, median, add 1, median

hints: Sorting after every addition is far too slow; the median only needs the middle of the data.
Keep the smaller half in a max-heap and the larger half in a min-heap, and rebalance so their sizes differ by at most one.

The median is the top of the larger heap, or the average of both tops (computed in a wider type) when the sizes are equal. Intended complexity: O(log n) per add and O(1) per median, so a stream of n additions with medians costs O(n log n) time and O(n) space, where n is the number of values added.
inputSyntax: Input: operations separated by commas, for example: add 5, add 15, median, add 1, median
